mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (GDPC1) create a dual labor-market stress that elevates risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while GDPC1 decreases over the prior month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test shows no significant predictive relationship between the combined proxy and SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500K units signals accelerating domestic demand, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed expansionary housing periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) above 105 suggests supply-side acceleration that, when combined with falling inflation (CPIAUCSL < 260), supports a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 260
failure_condition: No significant correlation between the combined signal and SPX 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months during a period of rising FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative forward returns over the next 60 days as higher discount rates erode equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.0 and FEDFUNDS increasing for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with the combined trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200K while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4% creates a labor market imbalance that predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200K and UNRATE < 4.0 for the current month
failure_condition: No significant predictive power in OLS regression (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in general inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for 10 consecutive months, regardless of other signals, is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to reduced discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly higher than the 60-day rolling mean during confirmed low-inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 1.5% for three months, it indicates accommodative monetary policy that tends to support equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no significant positive relationship with the duration of below-1.5% FEDFUNDS (p > 0.05).
